name: Greater Romania
summary: Greater Romania is the Romanian nationalist ideal of uniting all Romanians in one state, first realised in 1918 with Transylvania, Bessarabia and Bukovina and lost in part in 1940. Today it survives as irredentism toward Moldova and parts of Ukraine, most visibly in the Greater Romania Party. Adherents combine ethnic nationalism, Orthodox-tinged social conservatism, and a state-centred, populist approach to the economy.
scope: Greater Romania as the defining sources present it: the Romanian nation-state of 1918-1940 that united Transylvania, Bukovina, Bessarabia and the Banat with the old Kingdom and so 'encompassed the majority of Romanians' (Britannica), together with the nationalist ideal behind it, a state of all Romanians whose unity aspirations ran from the mid-19th century to 1918 (Chelaru), defined in ethnic terms in the interwar period (New Europe College proceedings). Its modern strand is the aim of reuniting Romania with the lost territories of Bessarabia and Bukovina, voiced by the Greater Romania Party and the New Right (Cinpoeş). Excludes the Iron Guard's fascist programme and the Antonescu regime as separate strands, and the 1918 resolution text, which no defining source names as the ideology's canonical document.

missingStatements.text: A state may claim territory outside its borders because people of its nationality live there.
missingStatements.rationale: Greater Romania demands uniting Romanian-populated lands in neighbouring states, the ideal summed up as from the Dniester to the Tisza.

missingStatements.text: A political party representing an ethnic minority should be banned if it is suspected of working to separate a region from the country.
missingStatements.rationale: The Greater Romania Party called for outlawing the ethnic Hungarian party UDMR, accusing it of plotting Transylvanian secession.

notes: Later pass 2026-11-24. The earlier answers rested on Wikipedia pages (s1, s2, s4, s5) and an untied primary text (s3), so they were nulled; the sources stay listed for the answer histories. Only four statements are answered, from Britannica (s6), Chelaru (s9) and Cinpoes (s8): union of all Romanians in one state, claim to co-ethnic land beyond the borders, return of Bessarabia and Bukovina, refusal of Hungarian territorial autonomy. Themes searched: territory and nation (Britannica, New Europe College proceedings, Chelaru, Eurozine), economy, government, religion, education, society (Britannica, New Europe College proceedings, Cinpoes), modern strand (Cinpoes). Livezeanu's Cultural Politics in Greater Romania, the icr.ro and usc.edu essays on interwar ideology and the 2026 Journal of Borderlands Studies article could not be opened (paywall, dead links, blocked). The sources that open describe the interwar state's schoolbooks, politics and economy, or the modern parties, not the ideology's own programme, so most themes have no stated position; the record may hold no more.

keyFigures.role: Founder and leader of the Greater Romania Party, which pursues reunion with the lost territories
